use_case_summary: Primary workload: low-latency user-facing chat for ad-personalization and real-time reranking of candidate ads. High QPS during spikes; strict P95 latency target of <120ms for short contexts. Secondary: embedding extraction for recall and personalization embeddings.
notes:
- Account summary: Enterprise adtech platform evaluating Redwood Private and Dedicated for inference tier. After 6 months of evaluation they elected to self-host open-source stacks (vLLM for batching/KV cache, TGI for model serving, TensorRT-LLM for optimized GPU kernels) due to cost and control.
- Technical reasoning captured on calls: want kernel-level tuning (TensorRT) and ability to control NCCL/PCIe placement, custom quantization knobs, and direct access to KVM-level GPU telemetry. Quote from CTO: "We need root-level kernel control to hit our SLOs and squeeze cost out of the fleet."
- Security: initial security checklist nearly complete, but final air-gap and HSM integration required additional project approvals; procurement cited higher up-front OPEX/CapEx favorable for in-house deployment.
- POC notes: Cascade ran a 3-week POC with 2xA100 nodes running vLLM + TGI; observed promising latency but wanted deeper TensorRT tuning. Their infra team felt comfortable operationalizing.
- Sales context: AE pushed Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, quant profiles) and Dedicated reserved options; engineering team prioritized long-term ops ownership.
- Current state: Closed-lost to internal self-host. Recommend 'keep warm' cadence: quarterly check-ins, monitor for infra cost signals, reach out if they rebalance to managed or need observability plug-ins.
- Suggested collateral to leave: private deployment runbook, integration checklist for KMS/HSM, comparative TCO spreadsheet (links above).
- Internal notes: Miguel to capture kernel tuning patterns learned from POC and feed into Redwood docs for future enterprise pitches.
customer_quotes: We value the operational control — if we can tune kernels ourselves we can hit sub-100ms P95 at half the cost.
Managed vendor pricing looked good, but the CFO wants capitalizing on our GPU fleet rather than recurring managed fees.
